lines.text: Area or volume to change into another unit, such as $\text{m}^{2}$ to $\text{cm}^{2}$ → square the length step for area, cube it for volume ({{lesson:5.1}})
Lengths or masses given in different units → change them to one unit before you calculate ({{lesson:5.1}})
Area of a parallelogram, triangle or trapezium with a slanting side shown → use the perpendicular height, never the slanting side ({{lesson:5.2}})
Circle given by its diameter → halve it for $\pi r^{2}$ or $2\pi r$, or use $C = \pi d$ directly ({{lesson:5.3}})
Arc, sector or sector perimeter → take $\frac{\theta}{360}$ of the circumference or the area; for the perimeter add $2r$ ({{lesson:5.3}})
Major arc or sector, or a missing sector angle → use $360 - \theta$, or put the values into the arc or sector formula and solve for $\theta$ ({{lesson:5.3}})
Solid with the same cross-section all the way along → prism: $V = Al$; surface area is the two ends plus the side faces ({{lesson:5.4}})
Cone given its perpendicular height, curved surface asked → slant height $l = \sqrt{r^{2} + h^{2}}$ first, then $\pi r l$ ({{lesson:5.4}})
Missing length from a known area or volume → put the value into the formula and solve; square root for $r^{2}$, cube root for $r^{3}$ ({{lesson:5.2}}, {{lesson:5.4}})
Shape made of pieces, or with a piece cut out → split into simple shapes, add, subtract the hole; for the perimeter count only the edges you trace round ({{lesson:5.5}})
Solids joined together → add the volumes; for surface area leave out the area where they touch, from both parts ({{lesson:5.5}})

Frustum (a cone or pyramid with its top cut off) → volume is large solid minus small solid; for a cone, curved surface is large $\pi rl$ minus small $\pi rl$, plus both flat circles for the total ({{lesson:5.5}})
